metadata.name: sync
metadata.displayName: sync - Synchronize cached writes to disk
metadata.description: Flush filesystem caches to persistent storage

installation.note: sync is commonly available by default as part of GNU coreutils

overview.summary: The sync command flushes modified buffer cache data to disk. It ensures that all pending writes in memory are written to persistent storage. Useful before unmounting removable media or before shutdown to reduce risk of data loss.
when_to_use: Before safely removing a USB drive or unmounting a filesystem
After copying important data and before power-off
Ensure all buffered writes are on disk

syntax.description: Without arguments, sync flushes all filesystem caches. With FILE(s), some implementations sync only those files (GNU sync syncs everything).

examples.title: Flush all caches before removing USB
examples.description: Ensure all buffered writes are written to disk before unplugging

examples.title: Sync then unmount
examples.description: Flush caches then unmount the filesystem

common_pitfalls.description: sync only flushes caches; it does not unmount filesystems or eject media.
common_pitfalls.solution: Run sync, then use umount (and optionally eject) to safely remove media.

related_commands.description: Unmount a filesystem; run sync before umount when removing media
